source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Read one increment of an elementary Itô integral. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
On any cell of an adapted dyadic elementary integrand's own grid, its completed Itô integral increment agrees almost surely with the cell coefficient times the corresponding Brownian increment.

On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is a dyadic elementary adapted process with its bounded, left-endpoint measurable cell coefficients.
The scalar driver is Brownian under μ relative to the given filtration. It is the driver for both the completed integral and the increment on the right. The chosen cell belongs to the elementary process's own grid.

I_{t_{i+1}}-I_{t_i}=q_i(B_{t_{i+1}}-B_{t_i})\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1}
  {Omega : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega} {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal m}
  {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure Omega} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Omega → ℝ}
  (q : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2Density.DyadicElementaryProcess filtration T)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration
      mu)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
  (i : Fin (2 ^ q.level)) :
  have I :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoTerminalCompletion.elementaryIntegrand q hB) hT hB
      hUsual;
  (fun omega => I (q.process.times i.succ) omega - I (q.process.times i.castSucc) omega) =ᵐ[mu] fun omega =>
    q.process.coeff i omega * (B (q.process.times i.succ) omega - B (q.process.times i.castSucc) omega)

blind_reconstruction.text: Let (Omega,m,mu) be a finite measure space with filtration F on nonnegative time; T>0; and B a scalar Brownian motion with F satisfying the usual conditions. Here scalar Brownian motion with filtration means centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B(t)-B(s) from F_s for every s<=t. Zero at time zero is part of the scalar law almost surely. Usual conditions mean that every mu-null subset of Omega is in every F_t, and F is right-continuous. Let q be a dyadic elementary process on [0,T]. It has a level l in N, N=2^l, times t_i=i*T/N for i=0,...,N (strictly increasing), and coefficients c_i:Omega->R, each strongly F_{t_i}-measurable and pointwise bounded: for every i there exists C_i in R such that |c_i(omega)|<=C_i for every omega. Its value is q(t,omega)=sum_{i=0}^{N-1} 1_{t_i<t<=t_{i+1}} c_i(omega). Embed this exact value process into the progressive L2 integrands on [0,T]. A progressive L2 integrand is a real process strongly progressive for F and in L2(mu product lambda_T), where lambda_T is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T], transported to NNReal. I_eta denotes its specified continuous completed Ito integral against the given scalar Brownian driver: the canonical limit of elementary integrals, set to zero on its exceptional null set, and held constant after T. For every i=0,...,N-1, I_q(t_{i+1},omega)-I_q(t_i,omega)=c_i(omega)*(B(t_{i+1},omega)-B(t_i,omega)) for mu-almost every omega.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess

/-! # Completed Itô increments of dyadic elementary integrands -/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralElementaryIncrement

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal BigOperators
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 ElementaryItoIntegral ElementaryItoProcess
  ProgressiveL2Density DyadicElementaryRefinement ItoIntegralProcess ItoTerminalCompletion

/-- On an elementary integrand's own grid, its completed Itô increment is the
cell coefficient times the increment of its driving Brownian motion. -/
theorem itoIntegralProcess_elementary_grid_increment_ae
    {Omega : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega}
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 m} {mu : Measure Omega} [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    {T : ℝ≥0} {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ}
    (q : DyadicElementaryProcess filtration T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) (i : Fin (2 ^ q.level)) :
    let I := itoIntegralProcess (elementaryIntegrand q hB) hT hB hUsual
    (fun omega => I (q.process.times i.succ) omega -
      I (q.process.times i.castSucc) omega) =ᵐ[mu]
      fun omega => q.process.coeff i omega *
        (B (q.process.times i.succ) omega - B (q.process.times i.castSucc) omega) := by
  intro I
  have hlast : q.process.times (Fin.last (2 ^ q.level)) = T := by
    rw [q.times_eq, regularDyadic_last_time]
  have htime (k : Fin (2 ^ q.level + 1)) : q.process.times k ≤ T :=
    (q.process.times_strictMono.monotone (Fin.le_last k)).trans_eq hlast
  have hcomplete (t : ℝ≥0) (htT : t ≤ T) :
      I t =ᵐ[mu] elementaryItoProcess q.process B T t := by
    by_cases ht : t = 0
    · subst t
      dsimp only [I]
      rw [itoIntegralProcess_at_zero, elementaryItoProcess_zero]
    · exact (itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal _ hT hB hUsual htT).trans
        (itoIntegralTerminal_restrictAt_elementary_ae q hT hB (pos_of_ne_zero ht) htT)
  filter_upwards [hcomplete _ (htime i.succ), hcomplete _ (htime i.castSucc)]
    with omega hr hl
  rw [hr, hl]
  simp only [elementaryItoProcess, min_eq_left (htime _), elementaryItoIntegral,
    ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  have hmono := q.process.times_strictMono.monotone
  have hi : q.process.times i.castSucc ≤ q.process.times i.succ :=
    hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := i))
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · simp [hi]
  · intro j _ hji
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hji with hj | hj
    · have hjt : q.process.times j.succ ≤ q.process.times i.castSucc :=
        hmono (Fin.le_iff_val_le_val.mpr hj)
      have hjl : q.process.times j.castSucc ≤ q.process.times i.castSucc :=
        (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := j))).trans hjt
      simp [min_eq_left hjt, min_eq_left hjl, min_eq_left (hjt.trans hi),
        min_eq_left (hjl.trans hi)]
    · have hjt : q.process.times i.succ ≤ q.process.times j.castSucc :=
        hmono (Fin.le_iff_val_le_val.mpr hj)
      have hjr : q.process.times i.succ ≤ q.process.times j.succ :=
        hjt.trans (hmono (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (i := j)))
      simp [min_eq_right hjt, min_eq_right hjr, min_eq_right (hi.trans hjt),
        min_eq_right (hi.trans hjr)]
  · simp

#print axioms itoIntegralProcess_elementary_grid_increment_ae

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralElementaryIncrement

steps.title: Identify the endpoint values
steps.text: At a positive deterministic grid point, use the terminal restriction identity for the elementary integrand. At time zero, both constructions have zero value.

steps.title: Keep only the selected cell
steps.text: Expand the difference of the elementary sums. Earlier cells are complete at both endpoints. Later cells contribute zero at both endpoints. The selected cell gives the displayed coefficient times the driver increment.
